corpus_rule: Recent TASK-207 through TASK-240 excluding retired TASK-209/TASK-210, plus TASK-249 and TASK-252 through TASK-255.

retrieval_contract.search_mode: deterministic local lexical scoring over compact fingerprints
retrieval_contract.helper_access: helper packet only; no truth set and no broad repository search

scoring.retrieval_recall_at_6: expected task IDs present in algorithm candidates divided by all expected task IDs
scoring.critical_miss: an expected task ID absent from its query's top six
scoring.helper_selection_precision: helper-selected expected task IDs divided by all selected task IDs
scoring.source_choice_precision: helper-selected primary sources matching frozen expected source paths divided by all selected source paths
scoring.scope_adherence: no broad search, no non-packet repository inspection, and no writes
scoring.token_measure: ceil(packet characters divided by four), an explicit approximation rather than a model tokenizer

TASK-207.result: Preserved and hashed the generated bundle, extracted it reproducibly, and established an editable baseline before refactoring.
TASK-207.unexpected: The original HTML was a self-extracting artifact bundle rather than ordinary editable source.

TASK-208.result: Established the first multi-file app skeleton and paired screenshots with a dependency-free CDP interaction smoke check.
TASK-208.unexpected: The cheap screenshot-plus-interaction gate became reusable evidence for later HTML extraction work.

TASK-211.result: Audited rules against the parity-proven implementation and identified the replacement undo hidden-information exploit among the deviations.
TASK-211.unexpected: Undo saved state before revealing a random replacement, allowing a free peek and reversal.

TASK-213.result: Removed undo availability from the hidden-information replacement branch while preserving ordinary reversible undo and added focused regression evidence.
TASK-213.unexpected: A narrow behavior fix closed the exploit without changing the broader undo system.

TASK-214.result: Extracted the combat engine behind a ctx and window.CF installation contract while retaining seeded browser parity evidence.
TASK-214.unexpected: The module boundary made the unchanged engine loadable under a small non-DOM host.

TASK-220.result: Built a deterministic Node-based rule-engine matrix below the DOM using the extraction seam, real modules, a small host stub, and deviation-tagged cases.
TASK-220.unexpected: The existing modules required no application-code changes to run headlessly.

TASK-224.result: Built a deterministic proposal-only E/I sentinel, but retrospective recall was only one of four known insights.
TASK-224.friction: Transition-only signals missed positive architecture discoveries and corrections not encoded as typed durable events.

TASK-226.result: Ran a visible Discovery Agent against a pre-frozen ClearFront truth set and preserved known, refined, novel, weak, and drift classifications.
TASK-226.unexpected: The truth set supplies positive findings that deterministic failure-transition scanning could not see.

TASK-229.result: Recorded Pi's failed no-write communication requalification and kept it excluded from operational coordination and capacity.
TASK-229.friction: The terminal implied delivery without an observed outbound hcom acknowledgement.

TASK-230.result: Confirmed that exact acknowledgement text appearing in Pi's terminal did not produce an outbound hcom message event.
TASK-230.friction: Visible terminal output was not equivalent to agent-to-agent delivery.

TASK-234.result: Audited which Command Center checkout and template could update the operator-visible application before authorizing UI implementation.
TASK-234.unexpected: A correct template edit could still miss the operator-visible installed source.

TASK-235.result: Created a durable deployment-source manifest and repeatable provenance check for launcher, installed-copy drift, and listener uncertainty.
TASK-235.unexpected: Configured target identity and a currently running listener are distinct facts.

TASK-249.result: Made destructive-phrase matching clause-aware so prohibitions no longer classify safe read-only work as destructive while preserving imperative detection.
TASK-249.friction: A read-only task was blocked because its safety guardrail named actions it explicitly prohibited.

TASK-253.result: Preserved the ClearFront side-rails prototype and documented continuity, canonical-stat mismatches, validation steps, and asset-readiness hazards without touching production.
TASK-253.unexpected: Most square user assets were RGB images with checkerboards baked into the pixels rather than transparent RGBA.

TASK-254.result: Retired eight serial UI snapshot tasks in favor of one final-state Command Center review boundary with combined focused tests and live-template parity.
TASK-254.friction: One continuous feedback conversation had been represented as overlapping tasks owning the same files.

TASK-255.result: Separated governing-document navigation from generated historical retrieval and proposed token-bounded fingerprints, digests, and explainable waits.
TASK-255.unexpected: MAP already had most storage and governance substrate; the missing layer was compact ranked retrieval rather than another agent.

queries.question: I am changing card replacement and undo behavior. Which prior work found and fixed the hidden-information exploit, and what evidence should I open?
I need to refactor a browser game out of one HTML file while proving behavior did not change. Which work established reproducible extraction and a cheap screenshot and interaction parity gate?
I want deterministic game-rule tests below the DOM. Which prior task built the headless engine matrix, and which combat extraction exposed the ctx-based seam it uses?
A local Pi helper reports success in its terminal but fails to acknowledge through hcom. Which evidence defines whether it can take critical coordination work?
The E/I sentinel is missing positive architectural discoveries and operator corrections. Which pilot quantified that blind spot, and which discovery work supplies a frozen truth set?
Before editing Command Center UI, I need to know whether templates and the operator-visible installed app are aligned. Which audit and manifest should I consult?
A safe read-only task is classified as destructive because its description says dangerous actions are prohibited. Which fix addressed this false positive?
We have many rapid Command Center UI tweaks touching the same files. Which record consolidated them into one final review boundary?
Where is the preserved ClearFront side-rail prototype and the continuity warning about static stats and baked checkerboard assets?
Which plan separates navigation authority from generated historical retrieval and defines task fingerprints, workstream digests, and a hard discovery token budget?
